- const scope = opts.scope || DEFAULT_SCOPE; - const exportPriority = opts.exportPriority || "all"; - passed into buildVisitors helper. - Tests explicitly validate rule configuration schemas: - tests/config/eslint-config-validation.test.ts: - Imports validStoryReference and accesses validStoryReference.meta.schema[0]. - Test "[REQ-RULE-OPTIONS] rule meta.schema defines expected properties" asserts presence of storyDirectories, allowAbsolutePaths, requireStoryExtension. - Test "[REQ-CONFIG-VALIDATION] schema disallows unknown options" asserts additionalProperties === false. - tests/config/require-story-annotation-config.test.ts: - Imports requireStoryAnnotation and inspects its meta.schema[0]. - Ensures properties.scope and properties.exportPriority exist and additionalProperties === false.
6) Configuration validation & error handling (REQ-CONFIG-VALIDATION, Error Handling acceptance criterion) - JSON Schema-based validation via ESLint meta.schema: - Both relevant rules set additionalProperties: false, which causes ESLint to reject unknown configuration options with machine-generated error messages describing invalid config keys. - Typed properties ensure incorrect types are also rejected by ESLint's validator with helpful messages. - Tests confirming validation behavior: - tests/config/eslint-config-validation.test.ts explicitly names REQ-CONFIG-VALIDATION in the test title and checks additionalProperties: false on valid-story-reference, verifying that invalid options will be disallowed at config-parse time. - tests/config/require-story-annotation-config.test.ts ensures require-story-annotation has a similarly strict schema, so invalid options for scope/exportPriority will be caught. - Runtime config-loading error handling in eslint.config.js: - Dynamic plugin loading with fallback logic: - First attempts require("./src/index.js"). - If that fails, attempts require("./lib/src/index.js"). - If both fail: - In CI (NODE_ENV === "ci" or CI === "true"), throws an Error: "Traceability plugin not found. Expected ./src/index.js or ./lib/src/index.js to be present in CI.", failing fast. - Locally, logs a console.warn("Traceability plugin not built yet, skipping traceability rules") and continues with an empty plugin object, avoiding hard crashes while clearly signalling misconfiguration.

traceability.notes: The story 002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG is fully implemented. The plugin exposes recommended and strict presets via src/index.ts and these are verified by tests and documented for users. ESLint v9 flat config best practices are followed in both the plugin’s exported presets and the project’s own eslint.config.js, with detailed setup and troubleshooting documentation in user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md and docs/config-presets.md, covering JavaScript, TypeScript, mixed, and monorepo configurations. Rule-level options (storyDirectories, allowAbsolutePaths, requireStoryExtension, scope, exportPriority) are configurable and validated via JSON-schema-based meta.schema definitions with additionalProperties: false, and dedicated tests confirm these schemas, satisfying REQ-CUSTOMIZABLE-PATHS, REQ-RULE-OPTIONS, and REQ-CONFIG-VALIDATION. Runtime configuration error handling is implemented in eslint.config.js through controlled plugin loading with CI-failing errors or local warnings. CLI integration tests confirm that ESLint can run with this flat config and plugin without conflicts. Given this concrete implementation, tests, and documentation, all acceptance criteria for this story are met.
